title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 109
paragraphs: He immediately sent a messenger to one of Astyages' herdsmen who, he knew, grazed his cattle on the most suitable pastures in mountains full of wild beasts. The herdsman's name was Mitradates, and he lived with a woman who was also a slave of Astyages. Her Greek name would be Kyno (meaning "dog"), since her Median name, Spako, translates to the same thing—the Median word for dog being "spaka." The foothills where this herdsman kept his cattle lie north of Agbatana, toward the Euxine Sea. That part of Media, bordering Saspeiran territory, is very mountainous, heavily forested, and high, while the rest of Media is entirely flat. When the herdsman came with great speed at the summons, Harpagos said: "Astyages commands you to take this child and leave it in the wildest part of the mountains, so that it dies as quickly as possible. He told me to say this: if you do not kill the child and try to save it by any means, you will die by the most terrible death. I have been ordered to verify that it is exposed."
